newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fernandez pulls out of Argentine debt "road show".
newsitem.headline: Fernandez pulls out of Argentine debt "road show".

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez has pulled out of a U.S. and European "road show" to tout $4.0 billion of new Argentine debt to be issued this year because of "other commitments," his office said Monday.
His place will be taken by his chief advisor Carlos Rodriguez and his Financing Secretary Marcelo Kiguel.
Rodriguez leaves Monday night for London, where he is to see Bank of England officials and private investors, while Kiguel is to meet German bankers in Frankfurt Tuesday.
Fernandez's press chief Daniel Ponce said: "The minister is not travelling because of other commitments taken on after the trip was planned."

Ponce said Fernandez was likely to travel to New York Wednesday to meet the Council of the Americas and investors, and head on to Washington Thursay for the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

Fernandez won the support of the lower house of Congress to raise this year's total indebtedness by $4.0 billion, but still has to have it approved by the Senate. It is still not clear how much of that would be issued abroad. The government has confirmed it is considering a 30-year bond issue, or enlarging its recent 20-year mark issue.
